properties.name: Strait of Hormuz
properties.description: Gateway for Persian Gulf oil exports. ~20% of global oil trade passes here — 17–21 million bbl/day. Iran controls the northern shore.

properties.name: Bab el-Mandeb Strait
properties.description: Entrance to the Red Sea. ~5–6 million bbl/day. Yemen conflict and Houthi drone/missile activity have disrupted traffic since late 2023.

properties.name: Strait of Malacca
properties.description: Main Asia-Pacific oil artery. ~16 million bbl/day. Connects the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea. Malaysia, Indonesia, and Singapore control the shores.

properties.name: Suez Canal
properties.description: Europe–Asia shortcut. Saves 7–14 days vs. Cape of Good Hope. ~9 million bbl/day equivalent. Egyptian government authority (Suez Canal Authority) controls access.

properties.name: Panama Canal
properties.description: Americas oil and LNG corridor. ~0.8 million bbl/day. Drought conditions in 2023–24 reduced draft limits, forcing rerouting. Panama Canal Authority controls transit.

properties.name: Turkish Straits (Bosphorus)
properties.description: Black Sea oil outlet to the Mediterranean. ~2.4 million bbl/day, primarily Russian crude and Caspian oil. Turkey controls transit under the Montreux Convention.

properties.name: Cape of Good Hope
properties.description: Bypass route used when Red Sea is blocked. Adds 7–14 days and $1–2M extra fuel cost per voyage to European routes. Shipping surge here signals Red Sea crisis.
